paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this passage. Peter and John get seized, questioned and threatened, and the whole time they keep pointing to one name. Peter says, "Salvation exists in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to men by which we must be saved." (Acts 4:12) The healed man didn't stand there because of a trick or a talent, but by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth (Acts 4:10).

Now look at what made these two so bold. The council saw that they were "unschooled, ordinary men" and "took note that these men had been with Jesus." (Acts 4:13) Friend, that's GOOD news for us ordinary folks, because I was a quarter stamper in a junk drawer and the Most High still used me. Time with Jesus is what makes a person steady. Then Peter and John say, "For we cannot stop speaking about what we have seen and heard." (Acts 4:20)

And watch what the believers do when they hear the threats. They don't ask for a hiding spot. They pray to the God who "made the heaven and the earth and the sea and everything in them" and ask Him to "enable Your servants to speak Your word with complete boldness." (Acts 4:24, 29) Then the place shakes, and they are all filled with the Holy Spirit and speak the word of God boldly (Acts 4:31). So when speaking up about Jesus feels scary, baker, do the same thing they did: remember who He is, ask Him for boldness, and then go talk about Him. The story isn't over, because there's more to come for these believers.
